Subject: Kickoff: prompt mapping + canary triggers for VerdantAI QMon

Team — thanks again for the quick sync this morning. Follow-up notes and asks so we can get the handoff moving: 

Goal: get Redwood QMon integrated for our clinical summarization product with an emphasis on prompt-level regression detection and an automated canary/rollback guard. We want minimal manual monitoring on our side; primary ops should stay with Verdant AI but alerts need to be actionable and low-noise.

Immediate asks:
- Attach: prompt-mapping-v1.csv — this is our initial prompt set and sample golden outputs (rows: prompt_id, intent, expected_keywords).
- Can you propose a canary trigger matrix (what metrics, thresholds, time-windows) and an initial rollback policy we can test?
- We need eval harness integration: CI-based evals on each model deploy and a nightly regression scan. Point us to required webhooks/ingestion specs.
- Alert routing: we want critical regressions to page our on-call (PagerDuty), and informational alerts to a shared Slack channel.

Timeline: target a staged canary run the week of 11/12. We’re flexible but would like an engineering handoff doc and acceptance checklist by EOD 11/8.

Risks to call out: prompt variability across clinical cases (long sequences), and synthetic golden sets might not cover edge-case phenotypes. Happy to provide more labeled samples if you need them.

Thanks — Josh
Josh Levin
Head of Product, VerdantAI

Josh / Kate — thanks for the clear asks and the prompt set. High-level plan and ownership below so we can align on the EOD-11/8 artifacts.

What Redwood will deliver by 11/8:
- Canary Trigger Matrix (first pass): metrics, thresholds, and time-windows in canary-trigger-matrix.xlsx (attached).
- Handoff doc: step-by-step implementation playbook and acceptance checklist (qmon-evalhook-integration.docx).
- Eval harness integration spec & webhook example (also in the doc).

Who owns what (internal):
- Diego Fernandez: implementation of the evalhook + ingestion, CI job setup, webhook endpoints (Diego).
- Laura Bennett: CS acceptance criteria, operational runbook, alert noise-tuning and customer-facing runbook (Laura).
- Marissa Cole: onboarding coordination and go/no-go for the staged canary (Marissa).
- Me (Sergio): program-level owner and escalation contact.

Initial canary suggestions (short):
- Metric A: Prompt-level semantic similarity drop (embedding cosine) — trigger if median drop > 0.08 relative to baseline over 1h and sustained for 3 consecutive windows.
- Metric B: Top-3 token disagreement rate — trigger if > 6% over 30m.
- Metric C: Latency p95 increase > 2x baseline with concomitant error rate > 0.5%.
- Severity mapping: informational (investigate), warning (notify CS + eng), critical (auto-failover to fallback model + page on-call).

Rollback policy (proposal):
- Auto-fallback: if a critical trigger fires during canary, route traffic back to current stable model and pause deployment pipeline.
- Manual rollback window: if warning-level persists > 4h without remediation, require rollback or express mitigation plan.

Next steps for Verdant: confirm PD integration (PagerDuty escalation key) and Slack channel, and approve the first-pass thresholds so Diego can implement.

Putting the attachments in this thread for transparency.

Sergio Alvarez
Account Lead, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Kickoff: prompt mapping + canary triggers for VerdantAI QMon — implementation notes

Thanks — I pulled the prompt-mapping CSV and the canary matrix. Technical notes / implementation assumptions below.

1) Eval harness integration
- We’ll add a GitHub Actions job (redwood/qmon-eval) that runs on each model-deploy PR. The job will: run the eval harness against the provided prompt set, compute the configured metrics (similarity, token-disagreement, hallucination-score), and post results to the Redwood eval API.
- Required from Verdant: a stable sample set (the CSV is a good start) + a secure URL to push golden references if you want nightly re-evals.
- Webhook: Redwood will emit structured regression events (JSON) to a configured webhook. Example payload and schema are in qmon-evalhook-integration.docx.

2) Canary trigger automation + autotriage
- Automation: implement a streaming detector that evaluates rolling windows. If a critical condition is detected, the system will: (a) mark the canary as failed, (b) spin down canary weighting to 0, (c) trigger the fallback routing to the stable model, and (d) post an event to the webhook and create an internal incident.
- Autotriage: we will attach an initial classifier that tags regressions by likely cause: prompt drift, model change, latency/resource saturation. That classifier will drive notification routing (e.g., model-change regressions -> eng; prompt-drift -> CS + product).

3) Alerting & paging
- PagerDuty integration requires an integration key; we’ll map critical -> P1 page. Informational alerts will post to the shared Slack channel and create a low-priority ticket in your Jira if configured.

4) Edge-cases / cost considerations
- Long sequences (clinical notes) mean embedding-based similarity is more expensive; we recommend sampling windows (first N tokens + clinical entities) for nightly scans to reduce cost.
- KV-cache warmup can skew canary latency metrics for the first few minutes; canary windows should ignore the first 5–10 minutes after rollout.

Implementation ETA (first pass):
- 11/8: deliver CI job template + webhook example + canary matrix refined.
- 11/12: run staged canary (2% traffic) with monitoring on.
- 11/13–11/16: evaluation and tuning, then increase to 10% if green.

Let me know if we need to include additional telemetry (output-length distribution, entity-coverage) in the first pass.

Diego Fernandez
Senior Software Engineer, Platform
diego.fernandez@redwoodinference.com
